system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Status:** Internal analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team. This is not a mark-up and not a negotiated position.

**Caveat on the seller's package:** Harbourglass counsel describes its positions as "key negotiated positions" and "fair and balanced." Nothing in our file shows that any of them has been agreed, and under our playbook none is cleared unless it passes our own authority process. The Disclosure Letter also speaks as at 22 September 2026, which is about six weeks old. Every factual point below needs refreshing before we respond.

---

## 1. Summary of Departures

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority | Seller is at our conditional fallback without authority |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Much higher, and loses first-dollar recovery |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval) | Shorter, without approval |
| Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and de minimis | Fundamental regime removed |
| Limitations / reliance | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | No fraud carve-out appears |
| Disclosure | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public searches | Specific fair disclosure only | Rejected |
| Buyer knowledge | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew or could find in the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; qualifiers need named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion, rejected |
| Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent plus evidence conditions are met before Completion | Consent-on-delivery, rejected |
| Riverlark | Release to follow Completion | Payout at Completion; direct repayment; effective releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Post-completion release, rejected |
| Employee bonuses | Excluded from funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded | Excluded, rejected |
| Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified either way | Narrow, rejected |
| DD-006 incident | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way; preserve logs; investigate | Seller's characterisation adopted without evidence |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Seller's label is an assertion, to be tested |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; no unlimited liability, no resolution assumed | Seller treats as closed |
| Title | Share register at DD-012 is sufficient | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence | Internal register is not independent proof |

---

## 2. Material Issues and Reasoning

### 2.1 Liability architecture (Clauses 12.1 to 12.3, 13)

**Cap.** The seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m figure matches our conditional fallback. That match does not clear it. The fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. We should open at 25% / AUD 6.0m and not signal the fallback number.

**Thresholds.** The seller's de minimis (AUD 25,000) and basket (AUD 250,000) are five times our figures. The structure is also worse: under the seller's draft only the excess above the basket is recoverable, whereas our playbook gives first-dollar recovery once AUD 50,000 is exceeded. On a seller-favourable reading, a claim of AUD 300,000 would recover only AUD 50,000. We should reject both figures and the excess-only mechanic.

**Time limits.** 18 months against our 24. The 18-month period is also our fallback and needs Amelia Frost's written approval. The seller's clause 13 proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. It would let the general regime's limits bleed into fundamental and other claims, which our playbook prohibits.

### 2.2 Fundamental and Title claims

The seller proposes putting capacity and title warranties under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is the most significant structural departure. Title and capacity claims are core to what we are buying. Our position is a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. We should reject the proposal outright and keep the categories separate.

### 2.3 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

The seller applies these to "all Claims of any nature" and does not carve out fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. Our playbook requires a carve-out from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no party may waive it. This is non-negotiable and should be stated as such. It should be framed as a matter of principle, not as a point to trade.

### 2.4 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)

The seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. This is deemed disclosure of the whole record, which would let the seller argue we are on notice of anything in the room. We reject it. We require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties. The 1.4 non-admission language is standard and acceptable, provided it does not function as a route to reject the Buyer's characterisation of facts.

### 2.5 Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

This is a blanket exclusion covering anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. It is precisely what our playbook deletes. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. The seller's wording would arguably bar claims on the very matters we are now flagging in the data room (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006). Note that the Buyer's current knowledge of these items should not be used as a reason to accept the clause. The clause should be deleted.

### 2.6 Bluefen change-control consent (Clauses 3 and 6.3; Disclosure 2)

Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent. Three problems:

- Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent under our playbook.
- Consent-on-delivery means we could close without knowing the consent's conditions (clause 11.3) are met.
- The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent or evidence of conditions is in the data room.

Position: effective consent plus evidence that the conditions are satisfied, before Completion, as a condition precedent. If the consent is not obtained, we should have a clear walk-right or price mechanism; this is a decision for Amelia Frost.

### 2.7 Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 and 7; Disclosure 3)

Riverlark has about AUD 3.2m outstanding and the facility has not been repaid. The seller proposes a release "following Completion." Our position is a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Note that the seller's facility figure is "approximately" and dated; we need a current payout figure.

### 2.8 Employee bonuses and funds flow (Funds flow; Disclosure 5)

DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs which the disclosure does not quantify. The seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and excludes them from the funds flow. Our position: they must be either a specific line item in the funds flow or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. We should also insist on quantifying on-costs. The "agreed price mechanics" wording on the funds flow is not evidence that the bonuses are cleared.

### 2.9 Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; Disclosure 4)

The seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank verification of non-payment. Our playbook is to broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. We should not treat AUD 180,000 as either confirmed or disproved. We need the payment records and confirmatory assignment, and the indemnity should cover the wider IP title and transfer risk, not only the one payment.

### 2.10 DD-006 export and privacy incident (Clause 4.6; Schedule 6; Disclosure 6)

The seller describes this as a "preliminary operational matter" and "not expected to be material." Our playbook requires that we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. We should neither adopt the seller's "not material" framing nor assume the worst. Practical steps:

- Require preservation of logs.
- Require an investigation scope and timetable.
- Require regular written updates, and a right to be informed before any notification.
- Establish the exact scope (about 1,240 records, potentially including names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps) and whether any access occurred.

This should be handled through specific indemnity or pre-completion conditions, with the general regime's limits not applied to it.

### 2.11 Sandbar renewals (Supplier renewals; Disclosure 8)

The seller calls the AUD 330,000 aggregate "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure says the documents do not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should assess these on the evidence. We should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct from price. The seller's label is an assertion to test, not a conclusion to accept.

### 2.12 Tax and IP

The seller treats tax and IP warranties as "settled under the general regime." Our playbook keeps these open, assumes no unlimited liability, and assumes no resolution. We should reject the characterisation that they are settled and keep them as separate, open categories.

### 2.13 Title (Disclosure 10; DD-012)

The seller relies on the Company share register at DD-012. That is a supplied internal source, not independent evidence. We need independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence, for example registry searches, confirmation of share transfers and a check of any encumbrances over the shares. The seller's disclosure itself acknowledges the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

### 2.14 Other items

- **Office lease (DD-007; Disclosure 7):** Notice obligation identified; the material does not establish landlord consent is needed for the share sale. Confirm with the lease terms and seek a landlord confirmation if we are uncertain.
- **Mossvale (DD-009; Disclosure 9):** Assignment restriction exists; the material does not say consent is required merely for a share sale. Same approach: confirm against the agreement.

---

## 3. Recommendations

**Authority and process first**
1. Do not signal the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap or the 18-month period. Both need Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and neither has been given.
2. Tell the seller's counsel that the "key negotiated positions" are not agreed. Our response should be a mark-up, not an acceptance.
3. Refresh all facts from 22 September 2026, including Riverlark payout, Bluefen consent status, SOW3 payments, the DD-006 investigation and the bonus on-costs.

**Liability regime**
4. Open at 25% / AUD 6.0m general cap; 24-month general claims period.
5. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
6. Restore a separate Fundamental / Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket and de minimis.
7. Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, with no waiver.
8. Reject the "any limitation applies to all Claims" override in clause 13.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
9. Reject whole-data-room, Accounts, statutory register and public-search deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
10. Delete clause 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Specific conditions and indemnities**
11. Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery. Confirm with Amelia Frost the consequence if consent is not obtained.
12. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
13. Employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. No silent exclusion.
14. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain payment records. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way.
15. DD-006: require log preservation, investigation scope, timetable and updates, with a right to be consulted on any notification. Assume no confirmed breach or quantified loss in either direction.
16. Sandbar renewals: assess each on the evidence. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
17. Tax and IP: keep open and separate. Reject "settled."
18. Title: require independent evidence (registry searches, transfer records, encumbrance checks). The DD-012 register alone is insufficient.
19. Confirm the office lease and Mossvale positions against the underlying agreements.

**Next steps**
20. Put the mark-up and a list of open information requests to Harbourglass counsel.
21. Brief Amelia Frost on the cap, time-limit and Riverlark / Bluefen decisions, which need her written authority.
22. Track all items in a single issues list keyed to the playbook, with the DD reference and status of verification for each.
=== END ADVICE ===
